reason: The citation and the missing guard are real: scheduleReset() (ArenaInstance.java:180-188) checks only the resetScheduled flag, keeps no BukkitTask handle, and /hilltop stop (HilltopCommandHandler.java:242-255) has no state guard, so a second stop issued while reset() is between line 1356 (restoreStarted=true) and the completion callback succeeds in re-arming a runTaskLater at line 184, because reset() clears resetScheduled at line 1358. When the rollback has entries but is short (BLOCKS_PER_TICK=200, MapRestoreManager.java:69; the default delay is 5s = 100 ticks, arenas.yml:179, so under ~20k blocks finishes inside the delay), completeResetAfterRestore (ArenaInstance.java:1450-1463) flips restoreStarted=false and state=WAITING before the stale task fires, line 1355 no longer returns, and the reopened arena is reset a second time. The claimed impact, however, is materially overstated: WAITING/STARTING are excluded from journaling (MapRestoreManager.java:276-282 resolveJournal -> isRecordingState), so the reopened arena has no journal and the second restoreWithResult completes synchronously (MapRestoreManager.java:522-531 runCompletion inline), returning the arena to WAITING inside the same call; and completeResetAfterRestore sets sessionVictory=null (line 1453), so removePlayer's record() passes victory=null and StatsManager.accumulate increments no gamesPlayed/wins/losses (StatsManager.java:253-263) - no false loss statistics and no map wipe. The net reachable effect is a spurious ejection of players who joined the just-reopened WAITING/STARTING arena plus countdown cancellation, and it requires an admin to fire two /hilltop stop commands roughly 5-9s apart; that is an edge-case robustness gap, not a medium-impact wipe, so the severity is reduced.
